newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - German jobs data weigh on mark, stocks rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - German jobs data weigh on mark, stocks rise.

text.p: Rising German unemployment figures, showing economic growth is too weak to revive the jobs market, weighed on the mark on Friday but stocks stayed buoyant despite the well-leaked data.
Wall Street's firm perfomance overnight provided European bourses with an early boost, but financial markets were cautious ahead of key U.S. jobs data for May, due out at 1230 GMT.
Platinum zoomed $60 to $495 an ounce in early European trading, its highest level since 1990, while its sister metal palladium fixed at a 17-year high of $240.00, up $30.
Both precious metals have soared in recent days because of a supply crunch caused by delays in Russian exports.
The dollar steadied at higher levels after the German figures showed a seasonally adjusted rise of 56,000 in the number of people out of work to 4.358 million.

"The seasonal revival in the German jobs market stopped in May. As before, the driving forces of the economy are insufficient to bring about a turnaround in the jobs market," German Labour Office President Bernhard Jagoda said.

Economists said the jobless rise showed Europe's biggest economy was not recovering as fast as previously thought, endangering the government's drive to narrow its budget deficit and qualify for European monetary union.
The dollar was quoted at 1.7373 marks at 0915 GMT, more than half a pfennig up from late Thursday's European level of 1.7285.

"Relatively strong payrolls and soft labour market data in Germany point to dollar/mark really sustaining its current levels or even gaining upward momentum," said Ken Wattret, international economist at Banque Paribas in London.
Against the yen the dollar stood at 115.98 versus 115.65, its upside capped by a report that Japan's trade surplus would be discussed at the June 20-22 Group of Seven summit in Denver.

Analysts said they expected a relatively quiet morning as the market awaited the U.S. payrolls figures. Although a strong number was largely priced in, the dollar could still rally if the data pointed towards a rise in U.S. rates, traders said.
On European equity markets, both Paris and Frankfurt put on gains approaching one percent at one point, but London lagged with a smaller rise following the 35 point rise in the Dow overnight.
German shares broke through the key 3,700 point level for the first time in early bourse trade, the 30-share DAX index climbing to 3,702 by 0915 GMT.
With the market still underpinned by Wall Street, traders said the German jobless figures had little impact because some of the numbers had been leaked.
SGL Carbon led the losers, down 21.2 marks at 239 on news its was cooperating with a U.S.-EU probe into graphite electrode price fixing allegations.

French shares rose through the 2,700 level on the blue chip CAC-40 index on the back of the weaker than expected German unemployment data and comments by Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer that conditions would improve in the labour market.
The CAC was up 15.23, or 0.57 percent, at 2,706.08 by mid-morning after putting on big gains on Thursday.
SGS-Thomson fell 5.31 percent to 446 francs after a profit warning.
But retailer Pinault-Printemps jumped 3.9 percent to 2,640 after its general meeting on Thursday. Brokers Ferri said the group had made an excellent start to the year.
British shares firmed during early trade, bolstered by the firm Dow but still jittery ahead of key interest rate news later in the session.
The FTSE 100 index was up 13.4 points at 4,589.6 by 0915 GMT.
Trading was seen cautious in the run-up to a possible British rate rise, following the first meeting of the Bank of England's newly-formed monetary policy committee.

Cable & Wireless helped lead the market higher after its Hong Kong unit Hong Kong Telecom confirmed C&W was in talks with the Chinese authorities on possible co-operation, while bank Abbey National gained on fresh bid talk.
CURRENCIES AT 0915 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7373 marks and 115.98 yen compared with 1.7285 marks and 115.65 yen in late European trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0915 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 13.4 points, or 0.29 percent, at 4,589.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 15.23 points, or 0.57 percent, at 2,706.08.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 29.45 points, or 0.8 percent, at 3,702.48.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold fixed at $343.80 versus $340.80 on Thursday afternoon. Silver was 14 cents stronger at $4.94. Platinum was trading at seven-year highs after being fixed at $495.00 versus $442.00, while palladium fixed at a 17-year high of $240.00, up $30.
